title: ZAM
focus_question: How does ZAM keep people capable while AI takes on more of their work?

statements.text: ZAM turns everyday work with an AI agent into active-recall practice, so automation sharpens skills instead of eroding them.
ZAM rests on six beliefs: theses, not proven truths, that evidence may overturn.
Human and AI amplify each other, and their collaboration should evolve as the human's competence grows.
Per concept, collaboration moves from shadowing to copilot to autonomy as retention and stability grow.
Even in autonomy, the human gets periodic real practice tasks, not quizzes.
Delegating without understanding is a safety risk: people cannot act when the agent fails.
The best learning happens when the learner barely notices it, so the agent observes instead of interrupting.
Agent skills decay too, so the same scheduling applies to what the agent knows.
The goal is never to make the human unnecessary, but to make human and AI more capable together.
Forgetting is a signal that reveals weak foundations, and the system responds to it structurally.
A rating of Again tells the system where to focus; it does not mean the learner failed.
Automation without practice causes capability loss, in humans and agents alike.
Knowledge is a shared graph of concepts; learning is each person's own journey through it.
A concept and a person's relationship to it are different things and are stored apart.
Concepts build on each other in directed, acyclic prerequisite relations that are the same for every learner.
Learning works best inside real, meaningful work; isolated flashcards are the fallback.
A work session, not a flashcard deck, is the natural container for learning.
Learning something while deploying production leaves a stronger trace than flashcard number 47.
Mixing topics during review trains telling concepts apart, not just recognising them.
The learning kernel must not depend on any AI vendor, programming language or interface.
Published protocol fields are a covenant: new ones may be added, existing ones are never removed or retyped.
Learning is free to the learner when those who benefit from an informed person fund it.
ZAM connects funders and learners but never holds money, which keeps its fee at or below 1%.
Funded content always names who paid for it.
An AI-agnostic kernel holds all learning logic and never calls a language model.
The kernel has zero LLM dependencies; anything that needs HTTP is injected from outside.
The CLI is thin orchestration: open the database, call the kernel, render the result, close.
Every model and embedding call lives in the CLI layer, under src/cli/llm.
Scheduling is pure: the same card, rating and time give the same result on every surface.
By default, all data lives in one local SQLite database, shared by the agent and the Studio.
A library can instead live on Turso or PostgreSQL, behind the same database contract.
Machine-specific state lives in ~/.zam/config.json, never in the shared database.
Knowledge is stored as shared concepts; each learner's progress is a personal card on top of them.
A token is a shared practice item: its wording, Bloom level, domain and an optional source link.
A card is one learner's FSRS state for one token: stability, difficulty, due date and lapses.
A concept enters a learner's queue only once that learner has a card for it.
Prerequisite edges mean "learn this first" and connect tokens, never cards.
A token's Bloom level, from 1 to 5, shapes how its recall question is asked.
The central model separates learning atoms, alignments, curriculum bindings, practice items and cards.
Reviews use active recall, scheduled by FSRS-6 spaced repetition over a prerequisite graph.
FSRS-6 schedules every card with 21 trained weights and a 90% retention target.
SM-2 is the classic spaced-repetition algorithm behind early SuperMemo and Anki.
Again means recall failed; Hard, Good and Easy all mean it succeeded, with different effort.
Rating Again on a token with prerequisites blocks its card until those foundations have been reviewed.
Only direct prerequisites surface, never the whole ancestor chain, so one lapse cannot start an avalanche.
A blocked card returns once every direct prerequisite has been reviewed and is itself unblocked.
The review queue mixes domains and slots a new card into every fifth position.
Every rating records how it was answered: free recall, tapped options, or a chosen answer.
A tapped answer never books an interval longer than 20 days.
Voice mode reads cards aloud and maps spoken words to ratings, so review works on a walk.
Learning happens inside the AI agent people already use, connected to ZAM through MCP.
zam mcp is the preferred agent connection; the JSON bridge CLI is the fallback.
zam agent connect writes the MCP registration for eleven supported agent apps.
Every bridge response is JSON, errors included, and protocol.ts is its stable contract.
MCP Apps panels show recall, the learning graph and the knowledge base inside the agent app.
ZAM watches the work and quietly marks a step learned when the learner does it well unaided.
Screen capture needs two gates: the host allows the call, and ZAM's policy limits what it may see.
The Desktop Studio and the mobile apps handle setup, learning content and focused review.
Setup that learners see belongs in the Studio, never only on the command line.
Many learners never open a terminal.
First run stays light: optional upgrades never block getting started.
ZAM Mobile runs standalone on Android and iOS, with no desktop, account or network required.
Pairing a phone with a server library by QR code is an optional upgrade.
Local text and image generation is offered only on an NPU, a discrete GPU or Apple Silicon.
On a CPU, generation finishes but is too slow to review with, and slow reviews mean no reviews.
The desktop app and the mobile apps are built on Tauri 2.
On macOS, ZAM ships notarized with a Developer ID.
The Mac App Store's sandbox would cut the app off from the database it shares with the CLI.
Learning content comes from the repo's own knowledge base, curricula, open decks and shared libraries.
The OKF bundle in docs/okf holds living articles about what is true in this repository now.
OKF articles state current truth; the reasons behind decisions stay in the ADRs.
OKF articles can become learning tokens that cite the article and heading they came from.
Where a curriculum cell covers a learner's position, import goes through that cell first.
Where no cell reaches yet, the manifest-driven curriculum import is the fallback.
An import wizard reads Bavaria's LehrplanPLUS curricula for school learners.
The Open Library lists reviewed, openly licensed decks that are pinned and checksummed before import.
Anki packages and CSV or TSV files import without any model or network call.
In a team library, newcomers start by taking topics the library already holds as their own cards.
